        description = "Detects embedded Cobalt Strike beacon configuration in memory or files"
        author = "SOC Team"
        severity = "critical"
    strings:
        $a = { 6A 00 68 [2] 00 00 68 [2] 00 00 6A 00 6A 00 }
        $b = "windows/beacon_bind_tcp" wide ascii
        $c = "/news.php" wide ascii
    condition:
        all of them
}

arguments.summary: A critical data exfiltration incident was detected originating from host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42), involving DNS tunneling to external domain c2.evil-example.com. The attack began with a Cobalt Strike beacon deployment via suspicious rundll32 execution, followed by lateral movement via SMB and exfiltration of over 2.3 GB of sensitive data containing PII and financial records. The source of exfiltration was misidentified initially as 10.0.7.50 but traced back to 10.0.5.42 through correlation of IDS, EDR, and SIEM data. The host has been isolated and remediation initiated.

arguments.summary: A low-severity port scan alert from IP 10.0.5.14 (host WS-FIN-042) targeting 10.0.4.1 was escalated following correlation with historical IDS alerts and EDR telemetry. Investigation revealed that WS-FIN-042 was compromised and actively beaconing to a known Cobalt Strike C2 server (198.51.100.23:443). Additional malicious behaviors included encoded PowerShell execution, unsigned DLL loading via rundll32, and lateral movement attempts via SMB. The host, belonging to a finance user (jsmith@corp.local), had not been flagged earlier despite prior critical alerts. Immediate firewall rules were enacted to block all traffic to and from the host.
